title: Rust: Queue (FIFO)
description: Implement a queue data structure using VecDeque and the FIFO principle.

steps.title: Queue with VecDeque
steps.description: Create a `VecDeque<i32>` and use `.push_back()` to add 1, 2, 3. Print the VecDeque.

steps.title: Pop from Front
steps.description: Pop elements from the front of the queue using `.pop_front()` until empty. Print each value (FIFO order).

steps.title: Push Front and Pop Back
steps.description: Demonstrate that VecDeque supports both ends: `.push_front(10)`, `.push_back(20)`, `.push_front(5)`. Then pop from back and print.

verification.failureMessage: Push front/back and pop back, print the popped value.

steps.title: Custom Queue Struct
steps.description: Define a generic `Queue<T>` struct using VecDeque with methods `enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `is_empty`, `len`.

steps.title: Queue vs Stack
steps.description: Create both a Queue and a Stack, enqueue/push [1, 2, 3]. Dequeue all from queue and pop all from stack. Show the different order (FIFO vs LIFO).
hints: Use VecDeque for queue (FIFO) and Vec for stack (LIFO).

verification.failureMessage: Show both queue (1,2,3) and stack (3,2,1) output.
